x-k-k2-01.title: Who dey leave, who dey stay?
x-k-k2-01.goal: Choose correct goodbye based on who dey leave and who dey stay, notice situation where both leave, and write polite goodbye with thanks.
x-k-k2-01.material:
지우 na student and speak politely to adults. 지우 say goodbye three times. Check who walk away and who stay.

Scene 1: 지우 finish talking inside 선생님 room and walk out. 선생님 stay at desk.
Scene 2: 지우 and 선생님 leave school together. For gate dem walk different directions.
Scene 3: 지우 eat dinner at 할머니 house. Then 지우 go home. 할머니 stay home.
x-k-k2-01.thinking.1: Handle case wey break simple rule
x-k-k2-01.thinking.2: Make polite goodbye for new situation
x-k-k2-01.prereq.1: Know 안녕하세요 and that -요 endings polite
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.prompt: Scene 1: wetin 지우 say to 선생님?
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.hint.0: Ask: who dey walk away, who stay inside room?
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.hint.1: Choose expression for person wey hear am. Wetin that person dey do?
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.r.a: You check who stay and choose expression for person wey dey leave.
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.r.b: Na person wey dey leave you dey talk to. Check who dey leave for Scene 1.
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.r.c: Na hello, no be goodbye. Think wetin dey happen at that moment.
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.r.d: Na casual speech, but 선생님 na adult.
x-k-k2-01.s.s1.explain: Person wey leave say 안녕히 계세요 to person wey stay. 지우 walk out and 선생님 stay at desk.
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.prompt: Scene 2: both of dem walk away from gate. Wetin 지우 fit tell 선생님?
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.hint.0: Describe with words: where each person go after gate?
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.hint.1: Try di rule from Scene 1 here. E still work?
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.r.a: Na for person wey stay. 선생님 dey stay at gate?
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.r.b: Na casual speech, and e no show respect to 선생님.
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.r.c: Mostly na hello. E no tell 선생님 say una dey part ways.
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.r.d: You notice say listener dey leave too, so expression for person wey stay no fit.
x-k-k2-01.s.s2.explain: Here listener dey leave too, so 안녕히 가세요 fit. Simple rule ‘speaker dey leave, so use 계세요’ no work because nobody stay.
x-k-k2-01.s.s3.prompt: Scene 3: 지우 thank 할머니 for dinner and say goodbye. Write wetin 지우 talk in Korean (polite speech).
x-k-k2-01.s.s3.hint.0: Say wetin 할머니 dey do: dey leave or dey stay?
x-k-k2-01.s.s3.hint.1: Put thanks before or after goodbye; both okay.
x-k-k2-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I use goodbye for person wey stay?
x-k-k2-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: My whole answer polite (no casual endings)?

x-k-k2-02.title: Thank-you to friend, thank-you to teacher

x-k-k2-02.material: 서준 give book to classmate, and classmate write back: ‘책 줘서 고마워!’ Now 서준 teacher give 서준 book, and 서준 wan send almost same message to teacher.

x-k-k2-02.prereq.2: You don see 주시다 / 주셔서 as respectful way to say ‘give’ for teacher
x-k-k2-02.s.s1.prompt: Which version of ‘책 줘서 고마워!’ correct when message go to 선생님?

x-k-k2-02.s.s1.hint.1: Say each option as if you dey talk to teacher: which one no get casual language and keep meaning?
x-k-k2-02.s.s1.r.a: Thank-you word polite, but 줘서 still treat teacher like friend.
x-k-k2-02.s.s1.r.b: Verb show respect, but 고마워! still how you thank friend.
x-k-k2-02.s.s1.r.c: You change both verb about wetin teacher do and thank-you word.
x-k-k2-02.s.s1.r.d: 주세요 mean ‘please give,’ so now message dey ask teacher for book; meaning don change.
x-k-k2-02.s.s1.explain: Both verb about wetin teacher do (줘서 change to 주셔서) and thank-you word (고마워 change to 고맙습니다 or 감사합니다) show relationship, and meaning must stay ‘thank you for giving me book.’
x-k-k2-02.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite message for 선생님 in Korean. Mention book and thank teacher politely.
x-k-k2-02.s.s2.hint.0: Start with 선생님 or 책을 and end with thank-you word.
x-k-k2-02.s.s2.hint.1: Check how your sentence end: e end with -요 or -습니다?
x-k-k2-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I change both verb and thank-you word?
x-k-k2-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I go send this to teacher?
x-k-k2-02.s.s2.modelNote.1: Add short promise; no need 주셔서.

x-k-k2-03.s.s2.r.b: You see say reason help listener understand.

x-k-k2-03.s.s3.prompt: Rewrite lines 3 and 4 in polite Korean so dem match lines 1 and 2. Keep meaning.
x-k-k2-03.s.s3.hint.0: First change only endings, then read two lines out loud.
x-k-k2-03.s.s3.hint.1: Two polite endings wey you know: -요 and -습니다.
x-k-k2-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I keep both ideas (bus and next time)?

x-k-k2-04.title: Request wey get yes
x-k-k2-04.goal: Compare ways to ask for something at restaurant, then write your own polite request with reason.
x-k-k2-04.material: At restaurant 민아 wan water. She dey look at busy server. Here na some things she fit talk.
x-k-k2-04.thinking.0: Judge which requests sound polite and clear
x-k-k2-04.thinking.1: Make your own request with reason inside
x-k-k2-04.prereq.1: Know 주세요 mean ‘please give’ and 저기요 fit call person attention
x-k-k2-04.s.s1.prompt: Which ways of asking for water polite and clear? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k2-04.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine say you be server. Which words go make you happy to help?
x-k-k2-04.s.s1.hint.1: Compare choices: which ones make request softer and use polite ending?
x-k-k2-04.s.s1.r.a: Short words fit make sense, but dem sound like order.
x-k-k2-04.s.s1.r.b: You see say calling person first, adding 좀 and using 주세요 make polite request.

x-k-k2-04.s.s2.hint.1: Two endings wey you fit use: 주세요 and 주시겠어요?
x-k-k2-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: My request show wetin I want and why?

x-k-k2-04.s.s2.selfAssess.2: E polite from start to end?

x-k-k2-05.title: One phrase, two meanings
x-k-k2-05.goal: Use context to decide wetin 괜찮아요 mean in two chats, then write clear reply wey avoid confusing word.
x-k-k2-05.material:
Chat A (for shop):
점원: 봉투 드릴까요?
손님: 괜찮아요.

Chat B (for school; 민수 step on 하나 foot):
민수: 어, 발을 밟았어요! 죄송해요.
하나: 괜찮아요.
민수: 정말요?
하나: 네, 안 아파요.
x-k-k2-05.prereq.1: You don see 괜찮아요 and 주세요
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.prompt: For Chat A, wetin customer mean by 괜찮아요?
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.hint.0: Wetin clerk ask? Customer dey answer that question?
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.hint.1: Say wetin customer dey answer, then test every choice as answer.
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.o.a: Yes please, give me bag now.
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.r.a: You fit use meaning from Chat B by mistake, instead of shop context.
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.o.b: I feel much better than yesterday.
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.r.b: You take 괜찮아요 as health statement. Check again wetin clerk ask.
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.r.c: You use question 봉투 드릴까요? and see say word answer offer.
x-k-k2-05.s.s1.explain: Clerk offer bag with 드릴까요? and customer politely say no. After offer, 괜찮아요 usually mean ‘no, thank you.’
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.prompt: For Chat B, which pieces of proof show say 하나 괜찮아요 mean ‘I’m okay, no problem’? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.hint.0: Look at line just before 괜찮아요 in each chat. Na offer or apology?
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.hint.1: Read last line of Chat B. Wetin extra information e add?
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.r.a: You see say word follow apology, so e answer am.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.o.b: 민수 no offer anything to 하나.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.r.b: You see say nobody offer anything, so ‘no thank you’ no fit.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.o.c: Word na same as Chat A, so meaning must be same.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.r.c: Word fit change meaning with context; same spelling no decide am.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.r.d: You notice say follow-up explain why e no problem.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.explain: Apology before it, no offer and later 안 아파요 all show say 하나 mean ‘it’s okay.’ Spelling alone no tell meaning.
x-k-k2-05.s.s2.acc.0: Apology before it and follow-up 안 아파요 na direct proof; no offer only support am because e absent.
x-k-k2-05.s.s3.prompt: For shop, clerk ask ‘영수증 드릴까요?’ and you want receipt. Reply in polite Korean without 괜찮아요 and say thank you.
x-k-k2-05.s.s3.hint.0: Think: which word from first chat fit sound like ‘no’?
x-k-k2-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Clerk go know for sure say I want receipt?

x-k-k2-06.title: Casual talk, respectful talk about somebody
x-k-k2-06.goal: Guess relationship between two speakers from their endings, find where respect for third person still show, and write polite message to that person.
x-k-k2-06.material:
하준 and 지아 dey chat. 선생님 na their teacher; 선생님 no dey inside this chat.

하준: 지아야, 숙제 했어?
지아: 응, 했어. 너는?

x-k-k2-06.thinking.1: Separate how speaker talk to listener from respect for third person
x-k-k2-06.prereq.1: Know -요 / -습니다 polite endings and -어 / -야 casual endings
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be most reasonable guess about 하준 and 지아?
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.hint.0: Check how each person end their sentences.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.hint.1: Any of dem use 요 or 습니다 when talking to the other?
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.o.a: 지아 older than 하준 by some years, so he talk casually to her.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.r.a: Older people fit use 반말 to younger ones, but here both talk casually to each other.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.o.b: Dem just meet and still know each other.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.r.b: New people usually start with polite speech.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.o.c: Close friends of about same age.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.r.c: You use fact say both of dem use casual endings with each other.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.r.d: Chat itself say 선생님 na third person.
x-k-k2-06.s.s1.explain: Both use casual endings (-어, -야, 너는) with each other, and 하준 call her by name using -야. This point to close friends/peers.
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.prompt: Even in casual talk, which parts show respect to 선생님? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.hint.0: Which words in chat talk about 선생님?
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.hint.1: Compare 했어 and 하셨어: wetin dem add?
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.r.a: You see say added -시- in 하셨어 show respect to person dem dey talk about.
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.r.b: These na casual answers, and dem show closeness between two speakers.
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.r.c: You see same honorific again for answer.
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.r.d: -야 after name na casual and dey address listener, no be 선생님.
x-k-k2-06.s.s2.explain: 하셨어 use -시- to respect 선생님 while sentence ending stay casual for friend. How you talk to listener and respect for third person na separate things.
x-k-k2-06.s.s3.prompt: Now 하준 write directly to 선생님 to ask when homework due. Write his message in Korean (polite speech).
